useFor: A form of several fields: each field's label, control and hint, fields side by side, sections under a legend, and the row of actions that closes it.

combineWith.how: Short fields that belong together go two-up in a .sedna-grid--fit, which drops to one column when there is no room for two.
Each field's error under its own control, and a summary at the top when more than one is wrong.
A switch in a boxed section's legend turns its body on, as a dependent block follows its option.
A checkbox group is one more field in a section or a box.
On a form longer than the screen the actions row becomes the save bar, or sticks.
The whole page around a form: the page head, the sections and the actions that stay in reach.

notFor.text: A long transaction asked one question to a page
Editing values in the rows of a table
Laying out a page that is not a form
The fields of one record, only read

useFor: Telling the reader a value was rejected, or is kept but unusual, under the field it is about and in words a screen reader hears with the field.

combineWith.how: Above the form once more than one field is rejected, linking to each.
A rule about a whole section goes under that section's legend and edges its frame.
In a two-up row the message stays under its own field, and the row stays aligned at the top.
A rejected set is aria-invalid on each box, with the error after the legend.

notFor.text: A condition of the whole page, such as read-only or degraded
A receipt that something was saved
A file turned away from an upload

useFor: A long transaction as a run of pages: one question to a page, a task list of the parts, a page to check the answers, and a confirmation at the end.

combineWith.how: Above the question when the pages are few and fixed; an eyebrow's Step 3 of 5 when they branch.
Check answers is .kv rows with a Change link on each, and a card per thing added more than once.
The task list is a .list--tasks in a card per section.
A task's status that needs attention, in words: in progress, not started, a problem.
A rejected answer goes back to its own question with the error under the field.
A whole page around one step, in the app's frame.

notFor.text: A form short enough for one page
The steps of a process the reader watches
Views of one record the reader switches between

useFor: Keeping Save in reach on a long form, saying that the work is not saved yet, and asking before the reader leaves it.

combineWith.how: The save bar and the sticky row are the .form-actions row, with the same order and the same --split.
A form in a dialog asks before it closes with the same data-close-guard.
On a phone the sticky row stands on the bottom bar rather than under it.
The receipt once Save has gone through and the save bar has gone.

notFor.text: A form inside a modal or a drawer, whose footer never scrolls
Saving the cells edited in a table

useFor: A single line of text the reader types, such as a name, an address, an email, a phone number or a password, with its unit, its width and its state.

combineWith.how: Each input in a .form-field with its label above and its hint below.
A rejected value carries aria-invalid and a .form-error under it that says how to fix it.
A .meter under a new password says its strength, with the words in its label.
A search field in a toolbar is a .toolbar-input, its width set with a custom property.

notFor.text: Several lines of text
A code typed a character to a box
A date or a time
Picking from a known list while typing
A number adjusted one step at a time

useFor: A short code typed a character to a box, such as a sign-in code, a PIN or a recovery code, posted as one value.

combineWith.how: The row of boxes takes a field's label and hint like any other control.
A rejected code is aria-invalid on every box, all pointing at one .form-error.
The page a sign-in code is asked on.

notFor.text: A password
A long number with a format, such as an IBAN or a card number

useFor: Several lines of text, such as a note, a reason or a comment, with room to write it, a budget of characters and the people it can name.

combineWith.how: In a two-up form the text area takes the whole row with .sedna-span-full.
A .menu of people inside a .mention-field opens on @ and writes the chosen name.
A rejected text area takes aria-invalid and a .form-error, as a field does.
A compact dropzone under a reply's text area for its attachments.

notFor.text: Formatted text with headings, lists and links
Markdown with a toolbar and a preview
One line of text

useFor: A date, a time, a month or a week the reader enters: a single day, a from and to pair, a date of birth, or a span of time for a dashboard.

combineWith.how: The .datepicker a typed date field opens from the calendar button beside it.
A from and to pair two-up in one section, so the legend names the pair.
A dashboard's time range among the toolbar's filters, its refresh button at the far end.
The quick select and the absolute range open as popovers anchored to the input group.
The common ranges in the quick select are pressed chips.

notFor.text: A schedule of events on a grid
A length of time in days or hours
Upcoming events read as a list

useFor: Picking one answer, or a few, from a short list known in advance: a drop-down, a list box, or two lists the rows move between.

combineWith.how: In a .form-field with its label and hint, as any control.
A filter in a toolbar, sized to its value with .sedna-w-fit and the toolbar's small tier.
A required select needs an empty first option for required to take effect.

notFor.text: A list long enough to need searching
Several picks shown as chips
Two to five short options always in view
A set of options ticked on sight
Actions on a record

useFor: A field the reader types into to find and pick: one value from a long list, several as chips, a list the server searches, a tree, or free entries such as addresses.

combineWith.how: Each pick is a .chip with its dismiss button inside the box.
A .tree in the panel, in place of the list, for a pick from a hierarchy.
Skeleton rows in the panel while a server list loads its first page.
In a .form-field with its label and hint, as any control.

notFor.text: A short list read at a glance
A set of up to about thirty options ticked on sight
Searching the whole app from the header
Running a command by name

useFor: A yes or no, one answer from a few, or a setting that applies the moment it is flipped: checkboxes, radios, switches and picture tiles.

combineWith.how: A set of radios is a .form-section fieldset, so its legend is announced with each option.
A switch in a boxed section's legend turns that section's body on.
Several checkboxes that answer one question become a checkbox group, with select all and a count.

notFor.text: A set picked from a list, with select all
A view setting of two to five short options
An action that runs when pressed
Filters that narrow a list

useFor: A field whose answer is a set picked from a known list, such as the agents a job runs on, with select all, a count, an every option and a none option.

combineWith.how: A checkbox group goes in a section or a box like any other field.
A facet is a compact group with the count each choice would leave.
Skeleton rows while the items load, as tall as the rows coming.
The error after the legend and hint, with aria-invalid on each box it is about.

notFor.text: One answer from a list
More than about thirty options
Options that are pictures
A long set the reader builds up row by row

useFor: Changing a setting in place from two to five short options, such as a time range, a layout or a unit.

combineWith.how: A range among the filters, because it narrows the list; a layout switch at the far end, because it changes how the list is drawn.
In a form, a .form-section fieldset names the group with its legend.
AND and OR between a query builder's conditions.
A control that switches the layout of one graph.

notFor.text: Panels of content switched below it
Buttons that each do something
Many options, or long ones
A setting that is on or off

useFor: Showing a score as stars, or taking one from the reader in whole or half stars.

combineWith.how: A shown score sits in a list row's meta, the number beside it for the eye.
A score to give is a field with its label and hint, and a hint that says why when rating is closed.

notFor.text: A value against its limit
A choice between named options

useFor: Choosing files to send: a picker button, a dropzone that is also a picker, the list of what is attached, and a drop anywhere on the page.

combineWith.how: Each file's progress once it is sent, under the same dropzone.
The zone in a form section, closed by the form's actions row.
A rejected drop is aria-invalid on the zone, with a .form-error that names the file and the limit.
A compact zone under a reply's text area.

notFor.text: Files already stored, to open or download
Reordering items by dragging

useFor: A number set by dragging or stepping: a range with its readout, a span with two thumbs, ticks, a vertical fader, and a stepper with two buttons.

combineWith.how: Each control in a .form-field with its label and hint.
aria-invalid or data-state="warn" on the range colours its thumb and fill; the message is the field's own.
A stepper beside a field and a button keeps one control height across the row.

notFor.text: A value against its limit, only read
The progress of a job
An exact amount typed with its unit

useFor: Picking a colour: the platform's picker beside its value, a preset palette of named swatches, or a spectrum for any colour at all.

combineWith.how: Each picker in a .form-field with its label.
The hue and opacity sliders are .form-range inputs, with their states and sizes.

notFor.text: A status shown in a colour
A category told apart by colour

useFor: A signature drawn with a mouse, a pen or a finger and posted with the form, beside a typed name that signs as well.

combineWith.how: The pad in a form section that closes with the form's actions.
The typed full name beside the pad, for a reader who cannot draw.
aria-invalid on the field edges the pad, with a .form-error under it.

notFor.text: A name typed only
A document the reader uploads already signed
